messages:
alex_infra: Heads up — scheduling a maintenance window for the us-west2 GPU pool (az1) tonight 02:00–04:00 UTC. Plan is rolling reboots + NIC firmware micro-patch to address recent thermal-margin oscillations. We will cordon/drain nodes in small cohorts and backfill from standby capacity. Minimal expected disruption but please review.

oncall_bot: Maintenance ticket created: MN-4821 — scheduled 2026-03-21T02:00Z by alex_infra. Pager duty notified.

luis_network: Which exact racks/nodes are in scope? need to verify upstream peering doesn't see transient BGP churn.

alex_infra: Cohorts: node-az1-[101..106] (canary), then 107..128 in groups of 4. NIC patch only on GPUs with fw v2.3.7 -> v2.3.9. We'll pause between cohorts for 10m metrics review.

alex_infra: Quick runbook snippet:
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon node-az1-101
kubectl drain node-az1-101 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
# post-reboot sanity
ssh ops@node-az1-101 'sudo systemctl restart nv_peer && /usr/local/bin/kvcache-seed'
```

maya_sre: Are dedicated/reserved pools affected? We need to avoid impacting committed customers.

alex_infra: Not touching any pools tagged reserved:true. Dedicated pools are excluded by the kube-node-label filter in the runbook. Canary nodes are standard shared-pool only. Also plan: keep KV cache prefills and prefix caches active to reduce token-latency spike.

sam_ops: What's the headroom today? if we start draining 4 nodes at a time, do we have enough spare GPUs to hold steady?

alex_infra: Current free GPUs: 12/120 (~10%). If we drain cohorts of 4 (max concurrent out), worst-case holding 8 GPUs out for patching due to overlap -> expected headroom to drop to ~4%, so we will pre-warm standby capacity.

alex_infra: Pre-warm: spin up 6 ephemeral GPUs in us-west3 (burst pool) before 01:45UTC. Estimated cost delta ~ $450/hr for the window (~2h). If cost exceeds budget, fallback is to stagger more (2-node cohorts) and extend window.

ops_manager: Please draft customer-facing blurb for status page. Also add rollback criteria (error rate, latency, OOMs).

alex_infra: Draft blurb in thread below and pinned in #eng-infra. Rollback criteria: sustained gen error rate >1% for >5min OR p95 latency increase >200ms for >5min -> abort remaining cohorts and failover traffic to us-east1.

dev_deploy_bot: Canary deploy started on node-az1-101 at 02:05Z. Monitoring hooks: trace latency, gen errors, ivector drift. Alerts on slack channel: #eng-oncall and #eng-infra.

maya_sre: LGTM. tagging oncall for visibility @sam_ops @luis_network :thumbsup:

sam_ops: Ack — I'll watch the dashboards. If I see spike >1% errors I'll trigger abort and notify sales/CS.

luis_network: I'll run a BGP flaps simulation against the test-peers at 01:00UTC and post results here.

alex_infra: Thanks all. I'll publish full runbook + rollback playbook and attach link before 23:00UTC. If anything unexpected comes up, hit me or @ops_manager. :warning:
